task_and_failure: Decide which memory systems, embedders, rerankers, memory LLMs and local serving runtimes to retain, trial, defer or reject for the one shared Claude Code and Codex memory, after the user asked why ai-memory is 'the best' and why the stack runs stale models. Failure addressed: the production memory stack kept the defaults its systems shipped with, without re-screening, and the durable-memory layer's keep_but_compare verdict had no matched retrieval comparison. Two frozen packets went to blind Claude and Codex lanes; three roles went to a blind GPT-6 Sol judge in three presentation orders; the convergence table sets each row, two skeptic checks per row reviewed it, and neutral Mac measurements in the LongMemEval-S harness bound the memory-system and embedder rows.
discovery_provenance: The model-screen packet (sha256 1847b3a1a0508078076f8d114e9ea1a021a92f8322f8e13e4f2482ca18f5a51a) and the memory-system packet (sha256 31318b2121b387e4a478456a5b794e6bf1119d100f9cb3aeeb96c17f19e6e807) each went to a Claude Opus 5.5 research subagent with web tools and to Codex GPT-6 Astra through codex exec with live web search.

Neither lane of a packet was given the other's output or the repository catalogs. The Codex streams show 15 and 16 web_search items, none naming the excluded repositories, and each Codex return predates its Claude return. The memory-system Codex lane read the ecosystem-catalog skill's SKILL.md (instructions only; no catalog query followed). The Claude lanes' tool logs were not retained.

The coordinator wrote one stage-one convergence note per packet; the lanes agreed on the leading embedders and on Hindsight and Mem0 OSS, and the unions went to measurement. The coordinator's workflow then built nine blinded briefs (memory system, memory LLM and reranker, each in three orders defined by a key), ran a gpt-6-sol judge on each from the brief alone, wrote the convergence table, and ran two skeptic checks per row.

The judge never preferred the Codex return; its only non-SPLIT answers came in order b, where the Claude return was letter A and listed first. The table therefore rests on candidate positions that hold across all three orders.

Nine skeptic checks on seven rows refuted a claim or a next test; the recorder applied every such correction, named the LMEB source on every row citing it, and updated the rows C3 bears on after C3 finished (report-mac-descriptive.md). No decision changed. Pins were resolved afterwards through the GitHub and Hugging Face APIs, and the returns were sealed as JSON with their original hashes.

predeclared_metrics.quality_rule: Lanes: each packet's output contract (a ranked shortlist of up to 3 models per role or up to 5 systems, the benchmark replacements or adapters, and the risks, under 900 words). Judges: under 500 words ending with PREFERRED and RANKING lines. A row reaches adopt_within_scope only with NCE in our harness plus a pass of the memory-lane acceptance, so no challenger exceeds trial. Harness arms: the preregistered LongMemEval-S retrieval protocol (session-level recall_all@5 primary; full-session track n = 470 and official track n = 419; A6 oracle ceilings; the A2 rule with A5 cluster statistics and the A14 and A15.2 families). The Mac arms are descriptive and decide nothing (A15.2). Semantic quality and source truth of the discovery returns are not graded here.
predeclared_metrics.usage_rule: No savings claim. Native counters are recorded as reported and mapped to contract categories only where their scope is known (the Codex lanes and judges); unknown stays null and no new sum across runs is claimed.

limitations: Discovery only for every challenger: no candidate was installed, downloaded or executed by this record, and every lane or vendor figure is measured elsewhere or estimated.

The harness figures are Mac-platform and descriptive under A15.2. C4, production with the LLM reranker, did not run on the Mac, so the layer decision (A14) is open; D3's 12 Mac rows are excluded from every analysis; C3's rows 349 onward ran on macOS 27.0 (a 20-question drift check reproduced recall_all@5 on 20/20 and ndcg_any@5 on 18/20).

The judge is one model (gpt-6-sol) from the Codex lanes' family, working from the brief alone. It never preferred the Codex return, and its only non-SPLIT answers came when the Claude return was letter A and listed first, so a position or label effect cannot be ruled out; the table keeps only positions that hold in all three orders. No refuter was run.

The Claude lanes' tool logs were not retained, so their blindness rests on the packet instruction; the memory-system Codex lane read the ecosystem-catalog skill's instructions, though no catalog query followed.

The skeptic checks' outputs are not committed (they hold local paths); their corrections are listed in convergence.json and applied in the catalog decisions file. Optional wording suggestions from non-refuting checks were not applied.
Contract quality covers the output shape only. No process exit status was retained for the lanes or the harness arms; the judges' exit 0 is as the runner agents reported it.

Usage: only the Codex lanes' and judges' categories are known. The Claude lanes reported 414,369 and 303,563 subagent tokens with 130 and 129 tool uses; these stay native in usage.json because their scope was not established. The coordinator, the workflow's agents and the recorder are not measured.

Pins were resolved after the lanes and the table, from current release tags and Hugging Face main revisions; the Ollama manifest prefixes are the convergence writer's and were not re-checked. Production ai-memory is a local self-build, which conflicts with the official-artifact rule until the first official 2.5 release.
The convergence table predates A16 (added to PREREGISTRATION.md at 02:15 EDT) and C3's completion (02:32 EDT); both are recorded as dated addenda, and the rows C3 bears on carry measurement updates.
LongMemEval-S tests chat recall, not coding-agent memory (LongMemEval-V2, VibeMemBench); 50-session haystacks are easy, and a pooled-store run is a planned A16 diagnostic.

rollback: Nothing on any host changed. Revert the catalog decisions file, its decision-index registration and the identity counts, and the durable-memory layer's added evidence_refs and limitations; keep this sealed evidence as dated history. Each trial row carries its own rollback.
next_decision_changing_test: C4, production with the LLM reranker (A14): the layer decision needs it, because a layer candidate must beat both C3 and C4 and C4 did not run on the Mac. Then, on VelaNext under A15, A15.1, A15.2 and A16, one GPU workload at a time: the gates (oracle ceilings, slot smoke test, reference-output and batch-invariance), C3 then C4 (the reranker decided first), E1–E3 and F1–F3, the rest of the original family, H1–H3, G0–G3, X, and the A16 arms D2h, M2 and K1. A candidate replaces production only if it passes both the C3 and C4 families under Holm (α = 0.0333; A16 at 0.0167) with a significant gain of at least +5 pp, then the deployable-artifact gate where it applies, then the memory-lane acceptance (an explicit durable decision retrievable in its intended scope with cross-scope negatives, and recovery).
